Hunting Command and Control (C2) Artifacts

A threat-hunting investigation using Splunk to identify suspicious Command and Control (C2) activity on Windows endpoints.

Scenario

Following the suspicious activities identified during previous investigation, we suspect the attacker may be establishing Command and Control (C2) communications with the compromised Windows endpoint to remotely interact with the system, transfer additional tools and payloads, and execute further commands.

Environment & Tools

  • Operating System: Windows 10/11 Enterprise.
  • Telemetry Collection: Sysmon.
  • SIEM Platform: Splunk Enterprise.
  • Log Sources: Sysmon & Security Event Logs.

Hunting Overview

Questions to answer

What are we hunting for?

  • Windows utilities downloading external payloads (certutil, Invoke-WebRequest, etc..).
  • Outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from unusual processes.
  • Commands referencing external IPs or URLs.
  • File creation by suspicious processes or in unusual locations.

Where can we find this data?

  • Sysmon: Event IDs 1, 3, and 11.
  • Windows Security: Event ID 4688.
  • PowerShell: Operational Logs.

How can we analyze this data?

  • Correlate process execution and command-line activity with network connections.
  • Identify suspicious communications and related file creation.

Hunting & Analysis

During previous investigations, we found suspicious activities that may indicate C2 communication. We need to investigate further to identify suspicious network connections and file transfers.
